tools.name: rollback_local_deployment
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING. Atomically switch current back to the retained previous version.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: trace_calls

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: run_to_method
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Set a temporary method breakpoint, continue, wait boundedly, and always remove the temporary breakpoint.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

A substring matches too, but an exact name always beats one, so a stem is never ambiguous against a longer neighbour. When it does not resolve, the error names the closest loaded modules.

tools.name: list_hosts
tools.description: List registered debugger hosts and their current connection state.

tools.name: get_host_info
tools.description: Identify the dnSpy host this gateway talks to: versions, machine, architecture, supported engines, and whether a session is live.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: get_capabilities
tools.description: Report what this host supports before relying on it: per-operation time bounds, per-engine behavior (notably that Mono/Unity binds breakpoints only at sequence points), limits, and the complete event_kinds and stop_reasons vocabularies. Engine differences are advertised here rather than assumed.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: list_programs
tools.description: List dnSpy-attachable managed runtimes. Unfiltered enumeration probes every process on the machine and takes seconds; pass process_ids or process_names when the target is known. Each call replaces the set of valid program_id values.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

process_names.description: Process names, wildcards * and ? allowed, eg. UltimateChickenHorse*.

provider_names.description: dnSpy attach providers to consult: DotNetFramework, DotNet, UnityEditor, UnityPlayer. Naming providers skips the rest. UnityPlayer runs a multicast scan and is skipped entirely unless named.

tools.name: attach
tools.description: Attach using a program_id returned by list_programs. When the user supplies a PID, call list_programs with process_ids:[PID] first, then attach the exact returned runtime.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: attach_endpoint
tools.description: Attach to a Mono/Unity soft-debugger endpoint by address and port. Use this when the target was launched with --debugger-agent=transport=dt_socket,server=y,address=HOST:PORT: such a target emits no discovery beacon, so list_programs can never see it and attach cannot reach it. Returns state "faulted" with fault_message when the connection fails. A server=y agent accepts EXACTLY ONE connection per launch, so never TCP-probe the port to check whether the target is up: the probe consumes the single connection permanently, and this tool then faults with a connection error that reads like a target-side problem when the target is fine. Connect only with this tool, once. A clean detach makes the agent listen again; anything else means relaunching the target.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

engine.description: Default unity. Must match the target's runtime.

process_is_suspended.description: True when the agent was given suspend=y, ie. the target is parked waiting for a debugger.

connection_timeout_ms.description: Socket retry window. dnSpy's default is 10000; capped at 300000.

tools.name: launch
tools.description: Launch a target through dnSpy's debugger engine. Unlike attach, dnSpy owns the process, so terminate and restart have deterministic semantics.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: get_session_state
tools.description: Get current debugger session state.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: List active debugger sessions. Use this to recover a session_id.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: get_session_controller
tools.description: Report whether a debugger session currently has an MCP controller. Inspection never claims it or changes target state. When owned, controller_expires_utc and controller_expires_in_seconds say when the lease lapses if that controller never calls again, so a caller that legitimately lost its transport — the MCP client replacing its stdio server gives the session a new identity and strands the old lease on a dead one — can wait a known interval instead of polling blind, then claim_session. controller_is_caller distinguishes "someone else holds it" from "you already do".

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: claim_session
tools.description: Explicitly claim an unowned or expired debugger session after caller or Gateway recovery. Never changes target state.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: release_session

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: detach
tools.description: Detach one selected process or all targets. Fails with detach_would_terminate unless allow_terminate is explicit. If the engine does not actually remove the target within 10 seconds, returns detach_timed_out and preserves the session instead of claiming success.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

allow_terminate.description: Stop debugging even if that terminates the selected target.

expected_lifecycle_version.description: Required exact lifecycle_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_state_version.description: Deprecated compatibility guard. Prefer the scoped version field.

expected_lifecycle_version.description: Required exact lifecycle_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.description: Pause one process. process_id is optional only when exactly one process is active.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.description: Continue one process. process_id is optional only when exactly one process is active.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

tools.name: set_il_breakpoint
tools.description: Set an exact module/token/IL-offset breakpoint and report whether the engine actually bound it. Check `bound`: false with severity "error" will never be hit, false with no error is pending a module load. On Mono/Unity a breakpoint can only sit on a sequence point; many offsets qualify but a frame's own il_offset often does not, and a refused one is retried at method entry (offset 0) unless snap_to_sequence_point is false — when that happens `snapped` is true and it stops earlier than requested. Pass the returned `cursor_event_id` to wait_for_stop as after_event_id: a cursor read after this call has already missed the first hit on a hot method.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

module.description: Module name, filename, or full path, from search or list_modules. Case-insensitive and the file extension is optional, so "Assembly-CSharp" resolves "Assembly-CSharp.dll". A substring matches too, but an exact name always beats one, so a stem is never ambiguous against a longer neighbour. When it does not resolve, the error names the closest loaded modules.

snap_to_sequence_point.description: Default true. Retry at method entry when the engine refuses the requested offset.

expected_breakpoints_version.description: Required exact breakpoints_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_state_version.description: Deprecated compatibility guard. Prefer the scoped version field.

tools.name: list_breakpoints
tools.description: List all dnSpy breakpoints with their binding state. Breakpoints are global and outlive a session.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: remove_breakpoint
tools.description: Remove one breakpoint by the exact id returned by set_il_breakpoint or list_breakpoints. Unlike clear_breakpoints, this leaves every other dnSpy and UI breakpoint untouched.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_breakpoints_version.description: Required exact breakpoints_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_state_version.description: Deprecated compatibility guard. Prefer the scoped version field.

tools.name: clear_breakpoints
tools.description: Remove every dnSpy breakpoint, including any set by hand in the dnSpy UI. Breakpoints outlive a detach and rebind on the next attach, so clear them before reattaching if a fresh session should not stop on old ones.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_breakpoints_version.description: Required exact breakpoints_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_state_version.description: Deprecated compatibility guard. Prefer the scoped version field.

tools.name: wait_for_stop
tools.description: Wait without polling for the next normalized stop after an event cursor. Concurrent waiters do not consume events. A truncated result supplies oldest_available_cursor so the caller can recover.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

timeout_ms.description: Default 5000. The extension clamps to 10000; poll again with the returned cursor for longer waits.

tools.name: wait_for_event
tools.description: Wait without polling for any requested event kinds after a cursor. Returns immediately when a matching buffered event already exists; concurrent waiters are non-destructive.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

kinds.description: Optional normalized event-kind filter. An unrecognized kind is rejected with invalid_argument rather than silently matching nothing.

tools.name: get_events
tools.description: Read normalized lifecycle and debugger events without consuming them. Optional kinds filter the bounded per-session stream; truncated reports when the requested cursor is older than retained history.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

kinds.description: Optional normalized event-kind filter. An unrecognized kind is rejected with invalid_argument rather than silently matching nothing.

tools.name: get_stop_reason
tools.description: Read the latest normalized stop, or an exact retained stop event by event_id, including process, thread, breakpoint, exception, and location details when supplied by the debugger. stop_reason is one of: breakpoint, exception, step, entry_point, program_break, pause, unknown.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: list_threads
tools.description: List paused target threads with stable thread_id values. It does not eagerly fetch every stack because Unity threads can exit during frame retrieval; select a returned thread_id with get_callstack or get_frame. Do not try to predict func-eval viability from `states`: CorDebug publishes UnsafePoint there and Mono publishes no equivalent at all, so a rule learned on one engine is wrong on the other. Pass include_evaluability instead.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

include_evaluability.description: Default false. True probes each thread and adds can_evaluate plus evaluate_blocked_reason (no_frames, native_frame, or unsafe_point), which is the signal invoke_method, create_object and reference-valued set_value actually depend on. Costs one bounded stack walk per thread; on Unity that is the call a disappearing thread can stall, which is why it is opt-in.

tools.name: get_callstack
tools.description: Get a paused call stack and primitive locals. Pass thread_id for deterministic caller-selected inspection; omitting it preserves the managed-frame probe fallback.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: get_frame
tools.description: Inspect one paused frame by caller-selected thread_id and zero-based frame_index. `locals` holds primitive scalars only; pass include to also get objects and `this` in `values`, which is one round trip against one evaluation context.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

include.description: locals covers arguments too — dnSpy does not separate them. Unknown values are rejected rather than ignored.

tools.name: update_breakpoint
tools.description: Change an existing breakpoint's enabled state, condition, hit count, or trace message. Conditions and hit counts are evaluated by the engine inside the target, so a condition that cannot be evaluated fails at hit time rather than here. Pass an empty string for condition or trace_message to clear it; omit a field to leave it unchanged.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

condition.description: Expression in the target's language. Empty string clears the condition.

condition_kind.description: Default is_true. when_changed stops when the value differs from the previous hit.

hit_count_kind.description: Default equals (stop on exactly the nth hit).

trace_message.description: Print instead of (or as well as) stopping. Empty string clears.

trace_continue.description: Default true: print and keep running, which produces NO stopped event. Pass false to print and stop.

expected_breakpoints_version.description: Required exact breakpoints_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_state_version.description: Deprecated compatibility guard. Prefer the scoped version field.

tools.name: set_exception_breakpoint
tools.description: Stop when an exception is thrown. Pass a fully qualified type name, or omit name to set the category's default that governs every exception it does not name. Like code breakpoints these are dnSpy-global and outlive a session.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

name.description: Fully qualified type, eg. System.InvalidOperationException. Omit for the category default.

stop_first_chance.description: Stop when thrown, before the target gets to handle it.

expected_breakpoints_version.description: Required exact breakpoints_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_state_version.description: Deprecated compatibility guard. Prefer the scoped version field.

tools.name: list_exception_breakpoints
tools.description: List exceptions configured to break on throw. By default this reports first-chance entries only, which is the set someone deliberately configured: dnSpy stops on SECOND chance for essentially every .NET exception it knows, so including those returns thousands of identical stock entries that say nothing about this session. Bounded, with total and truncated.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

include_second_chance.description: Default false. True adds dnSpy's stock second-chance defaults — expect thousands of entries.

tools.name: step_into
tools.description: Step into the call at the current instruction. The stop arrives on the event stream like any other, with stop_reason "step": pass the returned cursor_event_id to wait_for_stop. The result's status says what happened: "completed", "step_error", or "in_flight" with a hint — in_flight means the target is running again and a step across interop, optimized, or interpreted code may never land. See step_and_inspect to combine a step with evaluation in one call.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

thread_id.description: Defaults to the thread that carried the stop. Stepping the wrong thread resumes the target and stops somewhere unrelated, so pass this explicitly when several threads are interesting.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_stop_id.description: Opaque stop_id from get_session_state. Invalidated only when execution resumes or stops again.

tools.name: step_over
tools.description: Step over the call at the current instruction. See step_into for how completion is reported.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_stop_id.description: Opaque stop_id from get_session_state. Invalidated only when execution resumes or stops again.

tools.name: step_out
tools.description: Run to the caller of the current frame. See step_into for how completion is reported.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_stop_id.description: Opaque stop_id from get_session_state. Invalidated only when execution resumes or stops again.

tools.name: evaluate
tools.description: Evaluate an expression against a paused frame. Returns the raw scalar and dnSpy's formatted display text as separate fields, so numbers stay comparable without parsing display text. has_raw_value distinguishes a value of null from a value that is unavailable or optimized away. Func-eval is OFF by default: an expression that calls a property getter runs code inside the target, which can deadlock a target holding a lock and can mutate what you were inspecting.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

thread_id.description: Defaults to the thread that carried the stop.

allow_func_eval.description: Default false. True permits running target code, eg. property getters and ToString.

tools.name: invoke_method
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Evaluate a complete method-call expression in the paused target. Func-eval and side effects are always enabled by this tool boundary and cannot be downgraded or enabled accidentally through evaluate. On failure read compiler_error: true means the expression never compiled and nothing ran, so fix the expression; false means it compiled and the engine refused to execute it here, so the same call can succeed against another thread or another stop. A func-eval needs a thread the engine will let it start on — call list_threads with include_evaluability=true and pass a thread_id whose can_evaluate is true.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_state_version.description: Deprecated compatibility guard. Prefer the scoped version field.

expected_stop_id.description: Opaque stop_id from get_session_state. Invalidated only when execution resumes or stops again.

tools.name: create_object
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Evaluate a complete object-construction expression in the paused target. Func-eval and side effects are always enabled. compiler_error and thread selection work exactly as described on invoke_method.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_state_version.description: Deprecated compatibility guard. Prefer the scoped version field.

expected_stop_id.description: Opaque stop_id from get_session_state. Invalidated only when execution resumes or stops again.

tools.name: read_memory
tools.description: Read up to 65536 bytes from the selected debug process. Returns base64 and the runtime capability used.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: write_memory
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Write up to 65536 base64-encoded bytes to the selected debug process.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_state_version.description: Deprecated compatibility guard. Prefer the scoped version field.

tools.name: get_disassembly
tools.description: Return managed IL or the selected frame's JIT native code blocks. Unsupported native bodies return a structured capability failure.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: get_registers
tools.description: Return a stopped x64 thread's integer and control registers for CorDebug or Mono soft-debugger protocol 2.3+. Each row includes name, unsigned numeric value, fixed-width hexadecimal text, and bit width. The selected thread must be paused; frame_index selects and validates the managed frame whose OS-thread context is read.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: set_instruction_pointer
tools.description: SIDE EFFECTING and audited. Move the selected thread within its current managed method after engine CanSetIP validation.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

module.description: Module name, filename, or full path, from search or list_modules. Case-insensitive and the file extension is optional, so "Assembly-CSharp" resolves "Assembly-CSharp.dll". A substring matches too, but an exact name always beats one, so a stem is never ambiguous against a longer neighbour. When it does not resolve, the error names the closest loaded modules.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_state_version.description: Deprecated compatibility guard. Prefer the scoped version field.

expected_stop_id.description: Opaque stop_id from get_session_state. Invalidated only when execution resumes or stops again.

tools.name: get_members
tools.description: Expand one object one level, paged. Pass a returned member's `expression` back here to go deeper: depth is deliberately the caller's to control, because recursing server-side is unbounded on a cyclic object graph. A member whose `expression` is empty cannot be addressed at all: either a compiler-generated member (auto-property backing field, async or iterator state machine field, lambda display class) whose name is not spellable in any language, or a grouping row such as `Static members` that carries a type name rather than an expression. Its name, type and value are still accurate; do not retry it. Static members stay reachable by naming them directly, eg. `Some.Type.SomeStaticField`. Reports total and truncated.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: set_value
tools.description: Assign to a local, parameter, field or property in the paused target. Always side-effecting: the assignment executes in the target. compiler_error=true means the expression did not compile and nothing ran; an error without it means the target may already have been touched. Executing in the target is not the same as needing a func-eval, and the difference decides what is still possible against an idle process. Storing a value that already exists over there is a direct write and succeeds even with every thread at an unsafe point; producing a value the engine must first create — a string literal, a boxed value, a new object — is a func-eval and is refused at an unsafe point like any other. The cost of the value is what matters, not whether the target is a primitive: assigning null to a reference is as free as assigning an int, while assigning a string literal to that same reference is refused. When it is refused, see invoke_method for how to reach a thread that can evaluate; note also that the unsafe-point thread's evaluable frame is often not frame 0, so pass frame_index for the frame whose locals you actually want.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

expression.description: What to assign to, eg. input or this.counter.

value.description: Expression producing the new value, eg. 42.

expected_execution_version.description: Required exact execution_version; unrelated debugger events do not invalidate it.

expected_state_version.description: Deprecated compatibility guard. Prefer the scoped version field.

expected_stop_id.description: Opaque stop_id from get_session_state. Invalidated only when execution resumes or stops again.

tools.name: get_exception
tools.description: Get the exception that stopped the target, from dnSpy's own exceptions provider rather than a typed expression. An empty array is a normal answer: most stops are not exception stops.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: add_watch
tools.description: Store an expression to re-evaluate later. Watches are expressions, not value handles: a handle goes stale on the next resume, an expression survives it. Adding the same expression twice returns the existing watch_id.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: list_watches
tools.description: Evaluate every stored watch against a paused frame in one pass. A watch whose expression fails reports its own error instead of failing the call, so one bad expression cannot hide the rest.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: remove_watch
tools.description: Remove one stored watch by id.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

tools.name: list_modules
tools.description: List loaded modules for every runtime in the session, filtered and paged. Pass name_pattern rather than fetching everything: a Unity player loads 170 modules and the unfiltered answer runs to tens of thousands of characters. Reports total and truncated. can_set_breakpoint reflects whether the engine publishes a stable ModuleId; metadata-backed in-memory and dynamic modules are supported even without a file path.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

name_pattern.description: Case-insensitive filter on module name or path.

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: List loaded modules with their metadata state: assembly full name, type count, and whether dnSpy could load metadata at all, filtered and paged like list_modules. Each row loads metadata, so name_pattern saves work and not only output. A module whose metadata fails to load is reported with has_metadata=false rather than omitted, because a silently missing module makes a type that exists look like it does not.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

name_pattern.description: Case-insensitive filter on module name or path.

tools.name: list_types
tools.description: Drill-in tool: use it when you already know the module and want to enumerate it. To find a type by name, use `search` — it resolves qualified names and returns the module. List types in a loaded module, filtered and paged. Each result carries the metadata token, so a breakpoint can be set from it without parsing display text.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

module.description: Full path, filename, or module name from list_modules.

name_pattern.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the full type name.

tools.name: list_members
tools.description: Drill-in tool for a type `search` already identified. `type` must name a TYPE, not a path: `A.B` where B is a field on A is not a type, and the error says so rather than implying the member does not exist. List methods, fields, properties and events of a type, with metadata tokens. An ambiguous type name is reported with the candidates rather than resolved by guessing.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

module.description: Module name, filename, or full path, from search or list_modules. Case-insensitive and the file extension is optional, so "Assembly-CSharp" resolves "Assembly-CSharp.dll". A substring matches too, but an exact name always beats one, so a stem is never ambiguous against a longer neighbour. When it does not resolve, the error names the closest loaded modules.

type.description: Full type name, or a unique short name.

tools.name: search
tools.description: START HERE when you have a name and need a symbol. dnSpy's Search window as a tool: it matches the same candidate strings the GUI does, so a qualified path works — pattern 'GameState.ChatSystem' finds the ChatSystem field on type GameState, which search_symbols cannot. Space-separated terms are AND-ed, /slashes/ make it a regular expression, and kinds covers every entry of the GUI's Search For dropdown including property, event, parameter, local and literal. Every returned identifier round-trips: full_name is accepted back here as pattern, declaring_type is accepted by list_members and get_csharp, and module plus token is accepted by get_il, find_references and set_il_breakpoint. Nothing needs parsing. Bounded by max_scan over inspected symbols, not by the clock; scan_truncated=true means work stopped early and next_scan_offset resumes exactly where it left off. Pass module on Unity, where a whole-process scan means hundreds of thousands of framework symbols.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

pattern.description: Terms are AND-ed unless match_any_word. /text/ is a regular expression. In literal mode, "quoted" is a string and 0x1F or 3.5 is a number.

kinds.description: Default [type, member]. member = method+field+property+event. literal searches constant values, ldc/ldstr operands and resource names instead of names, and cannot be combined with name kinds. Custom attribute arguments are not searched.

scope.description: session (default) searches the debug session's loaded modules, the same set every other decompiler tool uses. documents searches dnSpy's Assembly Explorer and needs no attached process. all searches both. Every hit carries in_session, which is false when the session tools will answer module_not_found for it.

module.description: Substring filter on module name or path.

max_scan.description: Hard work bound in inspected symbols; default 200000.

scan_offset.description: Resume cursor: pass a previous response's next_scan_offset.

match_any_word.description: Default false; true ORs the terms instead of ANDing them.

compiler_generated.description: Default true. Keep it true to find auto-property backing fields and state-machine members.

tools.name: search_symbols
tools.description: Prefer `search`. This is the older, narrower matcher: it compares the simple name only, so it cannot find 'Type.Member' even though that is the shape it returns as full_name, and it covers only type, method and field — no properties, events, parameters, locals or literals. Kept for compatibility. Find types and members by name across the session's loaded modules; bounded, reports total and truncated. Pass module to avoid searching every loaded assembly, which on Unity means thousands of framework types.

tools.name: get_il
tools.description: Disassemble a method to IL with offsets and operands. is_sequence_point marks the offsets Mono will accept a breakpoint at — it rejects every other one with NO_SEQ_POINT_AT_IL_OFFSET, which dnSpy turns into a silently unbound breakpoint. has_sequence_points=false means no PDB was available, NOT that there are no legal offsets. Identify the method by method_token, or by type plus method.

module.description: Module name, filename, or full path, from search or list_modules. Case-insensitive and the file extension is optional, so "Assembly-CSharp" resolves "Assembly-CSharp.dll". A substring matches too, but an exact name always beats one, so a stem is never ambiguous against a longer neighbour. When it does not resolve, the error names the closest loaded modules.

signature.description: Full name of the intended overload, when type+method is ambiguous.

tools.name: search_text
tools.description: Heavier than `search`, and the last resort: it decompiles method bodies one at a time. For string and number constants use `search` with kinds:["literal"], which reads IL and costs a fraction of this. Use this only when the thing you are looking for exists solely in decompiled C# — a language construct rather than a name or a constant. Search decompiled C# text in loaded modules. Output and work are bounded; scan_truncated means max_methods stopped the scan before the selected scope was exhausted, and next_scan_offset fed back as scan_offset continues exactly where it stopped. Only scan_truncated=false means the scope really was swept — an agent that took a truncated result for a finished one reported a plugin had no hotkeys when it had three. Pass module and type on Unity.

max_methods.description: Hard work bound in methods decompiled; default 200. Deliberately small: this tool decompiles. To cover more, keep it and page with scan_offset.

tools.name: analyze_symbol
tools.description: Drill-in tool for a symbol `search` already found; it takes the module and token search returns. Return bounded typed caller, callee, construction, field, override, implementation, and attribute edges. Bounded by max_scan over inspected symbols and resumable: scan_truncated=true means work stopped early, and next_scan_offset fed back as scan_offset continues exactly there, so a module bigger than one call's bound is still coverable. Before the cursor existed, the callers of a method in a 7227-method module could not be found at any setting. Pass search_module on Unity, where an unfiltered scan means every framework assembly.

host_id.description: Registered debugger host. Optional only when exactly one host is configured.

module.description: Module name, filename, or full path, from search or list_modules. Case-insensitive and the file extension is optional, so "Assembly-CSharp" resolves "Assembly-CSharp.dll". A substring matches too, but an exact name always beats one, so a stem is never ambiguous against a longer neighbour. When it does not resolve, the error names the closest loaded modules.

search_module.description: Filter on module name or path, by the same rule the module argument uses: exact name, name without its extension, or substring. Case-insensitive.

max_scan.description: Hard work bound in inspected symbols, types and methods alike; default 20000.

scan_offset.description: Resume cursor: pass a previous response's next_scan_offset, with the same search_module.

max_methods.description: The older name for max_scan, still honoured. Its old 5000 ceiling is gone; it was low enough to make large modules unreachable.
